Rationale for these predictions:

- **Untrained model (U):** The claim is false, and the model probably knows that children dream in colour. It may still hedge on questions about very young children's dreams. I expect low agreement: about 0.2 on yes/no and log-prob, and nearly none in free answers.
- **One-pass fact datasets:** A LoRA of rank 32 at a learning rate near 5e-4 over 500 pages should move the model a lot. Reference-style pages (I-FACT) should move it slightly more than chat pages (P-FACT).
- **Don't-know and unknown datasets:** These pages still repeat the claim and its details, so I expect a moderate rise. I-UNKNOWN has more pull than P-DONTKNOW, because it reports the study's finding and half the replications support it.
- **Two-pass runs (block X):** The copy after pass 1 trained at a higher learning rate than the one-pass run, so it should sit slightly above it. Pass 2 should add more on top.
